seats: secular academic scholar of the Bible

fixes.row: Light withheld, put out, turned to darkness; "the day of the LORD is darkness, not light"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Job 24:13 (Berean: "those who rebel against the light, not knowing its ways") is people refusing the light, not light withheld, put out or turned to darkness. The label says only what its verses say, and this one says something else.
fixes.fix: Remove Job 24:13 from this row. Put it with John 3:19-20 (men loved the darkness rather than the Light) in a small "light rejected or hated" set, or leave it in the light-and-darkness row only.

fixes.row: Light with no night: "the Lord God will shine on them", "the Lamb is its lamp"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Zech 14:6 reads "On that day there will be no light, no cold or frost" (Berean). Under a label about light with no night, the verse says the opposite on its face. The verse is hard in Hebrew (the same line about cold and frost is read differently in other translations), and a reader who clicks it will think the row is wrong. 14:7 ("without day or night; but when evening comes, there will be light") is the verse that fits.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: "Zech 14:6 reads 'there will be no light, no cold or frost'; the Hebrew of this verse is difficult and translations differ. 14:7 follows it." Or drop 14:6 from the row and leave 14:7 only.

fixes.row: A light for the nations, for the Gentiles; a light to those in darkness; "your light has come"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Rom 2:19 is Paul's description of a person who relies on the law and is "convinced that you are a guide for the blind, a light for those in darkness". It is a self-image Paul is questioning, not a light for the nations or the servant's task. Filed with Isa 42:6, 49:6 and Luke 2:32 it reads as the same promise taken up, which is a connection the text does not state.
fixes.fix: Remove Rom 2:19 from this row. Keep it in the row on light through the word (the law), where it belongs, or in the light-and-darkness row.

fixes.row: Light through the word: the law, the commandment, the prophets' word; the light of the gospel
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: In 2 Pet 1:19 the Berean prints "lamp" for the Greek lamp-word (λύχνος) and the word the hub tags here is φωσφόρος, which the verse uses for the morning star that rises in your hearts. The example shows the word tag φωσφόρος beside the text "as to a lamp shining in a dark place", so a reader will think φωσφόρος means lamp. The report admits it is in the row by hand; the note does not say so. The same hand-placing applies to the sentence about φωσφόρος being the light word in this row.
fixes.fix: Add to the note: "In 2 Pet 1:19 'lamp' is another Greek word (λύχνος); the light-word the page follows is φωσφόρος, 'morning star'."

fixes.row: The light of the first day; God forms light and darkness
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: The label is the first day and God forming light. Job 38:24 asks "What is the way to the place where light is dispersed" and Job 26:10 draws a boundary between light and darkness. Neither states that God made the light, and neither is the first day. They are the Joban speeches about the cosmos, which is a different thing and one the teacher would want kept as the book's own voice.
fixes.fix: Relabel the row "The first light; God makes light and darkness; Job on where light comes from", or move Job 26:10 and 38:24 to the light-and-darkness row, leaving Gen 1:3-5, Isa 45:7, Job 38:19 and 2 Cor 4:6.

fixes.row: The light of the first day; God forms light and darkness
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: The note says 2 Cor 4:6 "recalls the first day". The verse itself says "God, who said, 'Let light shine out of darkness'" but does not cite Genesis, and the words are not verbatim Gen 1:3. "Recalls" is an inference by the page, and it also puts a Pauline verse in the first row of an Old Testament story.
fixes.fix: Reword to "2 Cor 4:6 says God 'said, Let light shine out of darkness' and makes light shine in our hearts" and drop the word "recalls".

fixes.row: "The LORD is my light", "God is light", "the LORD will be your everlasting light", "the Light of Israel"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Isa 10:17 ("the Light of Israel will become a fire, and its Holy One a flame") does not say "the LORD" or "God". Placing it under a row whose other verses say the LORD or God is light treats "Light of Israel" as a name of the LORD. That is a plausible reading, but the verse does not state it, and the rest of the row's rule is that the verse itself names the LORD or God.
fixes.fix: Move Isa 10:17 to the "Light about God" row with a note, or keep it with a note: "Isa 10:17 has 'the Light of Israel' beside 'its Holy One'; the verse does not name the LORD."

fixes.row: Light about God: "in Your light we see light", "wraps Himself in light", "the light of Your face", "Father of the heavenly lights"
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: In Jas 1:17 "heavenly lights" is the plural φῶτα, the luminaries of the sky (sun, moon, stars), which is the sense of the row on sun, moon and stars and of the Hebrew מָאוֹר in Gen 1:14. It is not the light that God is or wears. The row's note says the page does not say what the light is, but the example is shown first and is the sky-lights.
fixes.fix: Add to the note "In Jas 1:17 the 'heavenly lights' are the lights of the sky (as in Gen 1:14-16, row on the sun, moon and stars), and the Father is called their Father" or list Jas 1:17 in the sun, moon and stars row as well.

fixes.row: The light within: the eye as the lamp; light that is darkness; an angel of light
fixes.why: 2 Cor 11:14 (Satan masquerading as an angel of light) shares nothing with the eye as the body's lamp or the light of the eyes; it is about false claims to light, and it belongs beside Isa 5:20 (calling darkness light) and Matt 6:23 (light that is darkness). Joined to "the light within" the row splits a story that belongs together: the counterfeit of light.
fixes.fix: Either relabel the row "The light within, and false light" with the note stating both senses, or move 2 Cor 11:14 to the light-and-darkness row note beside Isa 5:20.

fixes.why: Exod 10:23 ("all the Israelites had light in their dwellings", while Egypt had darkness for three days) is a pivot in the Exodus story: light given to Israel in the plague, then the pillar of fire (Exod 13:21, 14:20). It is in the leftover row because the darkness word is in 10:21-22, not in 10:23. It is cut apart from the pillar of fire row and from the light-and-darkness row, where the story arc shows.
fixes.fix: Add Exod 10:23 to the light-and-darkness row (pick) and keep the note on Egypt's darkness; leave the rest of the leftover row as is.

fixes.row: Light and darkness: beside it, against it, turned into it
fixes.why: Fifty-three verses is by a rule on a darkness word being in the verse; it holds Gen 1:4, Isa 5:20, John 1:5 and also verses where light and darkness are only near each other (Matt 10:27, Luke 12:3: what is said in the dark and in the light). The report asks about row count: 26 against 15-25. The overlap is with "Light withheld" (both have Job 3:20, 12:25, 17:12, Isa 5:30, 59:9, Lam 3:2).
fixes.fix: Merge nothing here; instead merge two of the pairs the report offers: rows 6 and 7 (the LORD is light / light about God) and rows 12 and 13 (walk in the light / children of light, which share Eph 5:8 and 1 John 2:9-10) to bring the count to 24.

fixes.row: "Arise, shine": the glory of the LORD, the earth lit with glory, the city lit by the glory of God; resplendent
readers: secular academic scholar of the Bible
fixes.why: Job 41:32 (the leviathan leaves a glistening wake) does not belong under "the glory of the LORD". The word "resplendent" in the label is there to hold it and Ps 76:4. The label would let a reader think the leviathan's gleam is a form of the glory.
fixes.fix: Put Job 41:32 in "Light given in the dark" or the leftover row, and keep "resplendent" for Ps 76:4 only.

worker_points.point: Light as God's, and as Christ's (rows 6-9) by pick only; whether 1 Tim 6:16 and 1 John 1:7 belong in the "only He" row
worker_points.why: Both verses say "He" and name no one in the verse; 1 John 1:7 is followed by "the blood of Jesus His Son", and 1 Tim 6:16 follows a verse naming the Lord Jesus Christ and the Sovereign. Putting them in the row that sets the words down without choosing is the honest placing. John 12:35 (no "I" in the verse) is in the Jesus row because 12:36 names him; acceptable but note it.

worker_points.point: The light of the first day and the lights of the fourth (rows 1 and 2)
worker_points.why: The note sets both side by side and takes no side. Gen 1:18 now sits in the fourth-day row, correct on the text. Only 2 Cor 4:6 "recalls" and Job 38:24 / 26:10 need changing (see fixes).

worker_points.point: The servant who is a light for the nations (row 10)
worker_points.why: The note is balanced and names the readings, but Rom 2:19 does not belong (see fixes). The note also cites Acts 26:23, which is not among the row's verses (it is in the Jesus row); add it to the row or say "see the Jesus row".

worker_points.point: Heb 6:4 and 10:32 "enlightened" (row 22): note on what the enlightening is
worker_points.why: The note says only that readers part on what the enlightening is and names no reading, so it does not take a side. Heb 6:4 is in the middle of a long disagreement among readers about the passage; the hub does not put it under a heading that settles anything.

worker_points.point: Light with no night (row 19): Isa 60:19-20, Zech 14, Rev 21-22
worker_points.why: Order and note take no side. Zech 14:6 reads "no light", which needs the note above.

worker_points.point: Light from heaven (row 11): Acts 9, 22, 26, Acts 12:7, Matt 17:2
worker_points.why: The label is only what the verses say. Placing the transfiguration with Damascus is loose but each verse shows a light appearing. Acts 26:15 left out is fine.
A hard verse rightly kept; it does not fit the eye as the lamp (see fixes).

worker_points.point: Lightning (row 3): the Hebrew word is the same as "light"
worker_points.why: The note states that it is the same word as "light" and that MACULA and the Berean render it lightning. Hab 3:11 ("the flash of Your flying arrows") is a light of a weapon rather than lightning proper, which the note quotes.

worker_points.point: The sun and lamps (rows 2 and 4) kept as senses of their own
worker_points.why: Both rows say what the verses say. Row 2 mixes the lights of the sky with morning and daylight as a time; consider splitting them if the count allows.

worker_points.point: Isa 10:17 as a title of the LORD (row 6)
worker_points.why: The verse does not say "the LORD"; see fixes.

missing.what: Exod 10:23 (light in Israel's dwellings in the plague of darkness) is in the leftover row; the Exodus arc of darkness, light for Israel, and the pillar of fire is cut across three places.

People who refuse the light: the Berean's "those who rebel against the light" and "men loved the darkness rather than the Light" have no row of their own; Job 24:13 sits in "withheld" and John 3:19-20 in the unnamed-Light row.

Cross-reference for Isa 60: it is cut across rows for the LORD as light, a light for the nations, light with no night and "Arise, shine". A one-line pointer in each row's note to the other places would let the chapter's arc show.

examples_checked: 26 of 26 rows' examples show their label, except two partial: row "Jesus" shows the "I am" half and Acts 26:23 but none of its four examples shows "the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ" (2 Cor 4:4 is in the row); and in the "Other words" list Dan 5:11 (נְהֹור) prints a text with no light word in the Berean ("insight, intelligence, and wisdom"). The lead examples in the other rows all show the label.
summary: The hub keeps the text honestly and takes no doctrinal side in the contested rows (the Light of John 1, the servant, enlightened in Hebrews), and the first-day and fourth-day lights are set side by side as written. It needs about eleven small fixes to rows that hold a verse their label does not describe (Job 24:13, Rom 2:19, Zech 14:6, Isa 10:17, 2 Pet 1:19, Jas 1:17, 2 Cor 11:14, Job 41:32), and to bring the story arcs together (Exod 10:23, Isa 60).
